newsitem.title: MEXICO: Femsa to invest $280 mln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Femsa to invest $280 mln in 1997.

text.p: Mexican bottler Fomento Economico Mexicano (Femsa) plans to invest about $280 million in 1997, the company's financial director said on Thursday.
"We think the company's investments will be around the same amount as last year, about $280 million," Alfredo Livas Cantu told a news conference.
Livas Cantu said that of total planned investment, just over $90 million would go to the company's beer division.
"There are no plans for new production installations beyond the existing ones, but there are plans to increase production capacity at plants, with marginal investments," he added.

In the beer division, investment would also be focused on modernising and replacing assets at production installations, as well as expanding warehouses and distribution routes, he said. The same would be done in the soft-drinks division.
He said between $75 million and $80 million would be channelled to packaging, compared to $68 million in 1996.
Femsa planned to open between 75 and 90 new Oxxo convenience stores in 1997, in keeping with a recent 10 percent a year growth rate, Livas said.
The company would also invest $20 million to open 20 Amoxxo service stations, in conjunction with state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos, mainly in Mexico City, Guadalajara and Monterrey.
